Hi Jane — quick follow-up with the specifics you requested. I've pasted the short answers below and attached an updated CSV (same filename: subprocessor_inventory_2026-06-01.csv) with the new columns you asked for.

1) Audit window and bridge letter
- SOC 2 Type II report (Redwood) audit period: 2024-09-01 to 2025-03-31 (testing period).
- Bridge letter we provided is dated 2026-06-01 and states there were no material changes to scope or controls through 2026-05-31. Practically, that means controls tested in the 2024-09 to 2025-03 window can be considered representative through 2026-05-31. For runbook-level or configuration evidence after 2026-05-31 we can provide snapshots / logs if you identify specific control numbers to validate.

2) Cloud provider services we rely on (examples; full mapping supplied in the CSV attestation_url column):
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Compute Engine (VMs), Cloud Storage (object storage for transient model caches), Cloud SQL (managed Postgres for metadata), Cloud Load Balancing. We rely on the GCP SOC 2 attestation for infrastructure and underlying network controls.
- AWS: S3 (internal backups for a scoped customer environment), EC2 (in some dedicated setups), and IAM for multi-cloud integrations in a small subset of customers. (We primarily default to GCP in our hosted regions.)

Notes on scope: where we use managed platform services (Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage), the provider's SOC/ISO reports cover those infrastructure controls. Redwood retains responsibility for application-level access control, key management (we integrate with customer KMS when requested), encryption at rest for customer data, and log retention/monitoring configured in our platform.

3) Customer content vs. metadata/analytics
- The updated CSV includes a column processes_customer_content with Y/N values. Short summary of common entries:
  - Datadog: N (observability metrics and traces — we redact PII from traces in the pipeline)
  - Sentry: N (error telemetry for our service; no raw customer content)
  - Google Cloud Storage: Y (transient model cache artifacts may contain user prompts; retention is short and encrypted)
  - Stripe: N (billing, no customer content)
